Scope the release dry run's ref check to refs it can move (#290)

tools/release-dry-run.sh hashed the whole git for-each-ref listing
before its run and in step 6, so a ref that another worktree moved
during the run failed it, although the dry run had moved nothing (TODO
279, seen on the PR 284 gate). Step 6 now compares only the refs that
the dry run could itself move, read from the worktree that holds the
script before and after: the branch HEAD names, or that it is
detached; the commit HEAD resolves to; and every tag and note with its
object name. It prints both snapshots on a mismatch, so the failure
names the ref that differs. It then fails when a ref that git
for-each-ref lists from that worktree contains the dry-run commit,
read with replace refs turned off. The script names that commit before
git commit runs and fails closed unless git commit leaves the
throwaway worktree's HEAD at it, so a hook that moves that HEAD cannot
point the check at another commit. A git error in either check, or in
making or reading the dry-run commit, fails the run with exit 1 and is
never read as an empty listing.

This narrows a release-integrity check on purpose and needs the
maintainer's acceptance. Step 6 newly catches a commit on a detached
HEAD, and a detach or an attach at the same commit, which the old hash
missed because git for-each-ref lists no HEAD. The script's header
states what step 6 no longer catches, and what it does not see, in
these words:

Residual: the proof does not catch the deletion of any ref outside
tags and notes other than the branch the script's worktree has checked
out, such as another branch, a remote-tracking ref, refs/stash or a
refs/replace/ ref; a move or creation of such a ref at a commit that
does not contain the dry-run commit, or at an object that peels to no
commit, such as a tree or a blob; or such a deletion, move or creation
made by a commit hook, which the dry-run commit runs. It does not see
the HEAD or the per-worktree refs of any worktree other than the
script's worktree, the throwaway worktree included, or a ref outside
refs/ other than HEAD, such as ORIG_HEAD, of any worktree, the script's
worktree included, so such a ref put on the dry-run commit does not
fail it. It does not see anything the exit cleanup does, or a ref
moved and then restored between the 2 snapshots.

A graft file or a shallow file, neither of which is a ref, can still
hide a ref from the leak check. A write that another worktree makes
during the run still fails it when it is a tag or a note, the HEAD of
the script's worktree or its checked-out branch, or a listed ref put
on the dry-run commit or a descendant of it. TODO 279 does not record
which ref moved on the PR 284 gate, so whether this change would have
avoided that failure is unknown.

tools/test-release-dry-run-refs.py runs the whole script, copied byte
for byte into throwaway folders with stand-ins for the tools it calls,
so bash itself reads every line of it. Its 36 ref cases each build a
repository and make writes at 3 points: a git stand-in first on PATH
makes another worktree's writes before the dry run adds its worktree,
and, inside the dry run's git commit once it has made its commit, the
dry run's own writes, or in cases 28 and 29 another worktree's; the
stand-in of step 5 makes late writes after that step. Each ref case
checks that exactly the refs it names change. Its 8 cases on
fail-closed reading make no writes and require the run to end at the
read that fails. Residual of the test: stand-ins replace the
packaging, the gates and the site rewrite, which the next step of
release-dry-run.yml runs with the real tools, and the script runs with
a git stand-in first on PATH and an environment that the test fixes,
not those of that workflow. A change to the script is caught only when
it changes what a case observes, so a change that acts only outside
the cases, such as one that tests for the stand-ins or for the
workflow's environment, or that moves a ref no case writes or stops
step 6 reading one, is not caught. The cases run on 1 git version with
its default ref backend.

The test's first version of 21 cases, run against the unchanged
script, failed the concurrent cases and passed the detached commit;
against this change all 44 cases pass. Each of 14 mutants that remove
1 stated rule failed at least 1 case of the 33-case suite, each of 10
later mutants failed at least 1 case of the 36-case suite, each of 9
script mutants that the 36-case suite passed fails at least 1 case of
the 34-case suite and of the 35-case suite, and each of 13 script
mutants of the capture fix, 8 of which the 35-case suite passed, fails
at least 1 case of the 44-case suite. The release dry run workflow and
tools/run_all_checks.sh run it before the dry run, and
tools/test-run-all-checks.py records the new digest of
tools/run_all_checks.sh after a reading of the whole script. The
workflow header now counts 7 test suites.
